s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of painful lower-extremity nodules and polyarthralgia with systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Painful nodules on the anterior shins and inner left thigh
Edematous and tender left wrist, hand, and metacarpophalangeal joints with marked synovitis
Bilateral lower extremity edema with varicosities and exquisite tenderness of toes and dorsal feet
key_facts: 71-year-old man
Recurrent bladder cancer post-resection and local chemotherapy
Coronary artery disease
Essential hypertension with diastolic dysfunction
Tobacco use
Painful lower-extremity nodules and polyarthralgia developing over several months
Serum lipase >20,000 U/L
Amylase 7,914 U/L
Extensive autoimmune and infectious work-up negative
Cancer markers: CA 19-9: 118 U/L, CEA: 2.6 ng/mL
Multiple cystic lesions within pancreatic head on CT and MRCP
1.9 × 1.7-cm mass in portal vein with extension to superior mesenteric vein on EUS
Cutaneous lesion biopsy showing 'Ghost cells'—fat necrosis with saponification
Synovial fluid aspirate with no crystals, leukocytes, or bacteria on gram stain

shortlist.label: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum lipase and amylase, multiple cystic lesions within pancreatic head, and mass in portal vein

shortlist.label: Pancreatic lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic inflammation, painful lower-extremity nodules, and polyarthralgia

shortlist.label: Glucagonoma
shortlist.why_kept: Painful lower-extremity nodules and polyarthralgia, with necrolytic migratory erythema possible given 'ghost cells' on biopsy

shortlist.label: Erythema nodosum
shortlist.why_kept: Painful lower-extremity nodules and polyarthralgia, with biopsy showing 'ghost cells'—fat necrosis with saponification

shortlist.label: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Mass in portal vein, elevated cancer markers, and systemic inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's elevated serum lipase and amylase levels, multiple cystic lesions within the pancreatic head, and a mass in the portal vein with extension to the superior mesenteric vein are highly suggestive of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The presence of 'ghost cells' indicating fat necrosis with saponification in the cutaneous lesion biopsy further supports this diagnosis, as it is a known complication of pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Pancreatic lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma would not typically cause the extensive pancreatic lesions and fat necrosis seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Glucagonoma
rejected.why: Glucagonoma is a rare tumor that typically presents with a distinct syndrome of diabetes, weight loss, and rash, which is not described in this patient.

rejected.label: Erythema nodosum
rejected.why: Erythema nodosum is an inflammatory condition that does not explain the patient's pancreatic lesions, elevated lipase and amylase, or other systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor
rejected.why: While possible, the patient's presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with pancreatic adenocarcinoma than a neuroendocrine tumor.
